correctness.rationale: All n>=3 and t>0 covered. Constructed facet supporting normals give the exhaustive two dihedral orbits. Opposite monotonicities prove a unique crossing; the factored quadratic in s gives an exact minimizer. Independent face-pyramid volume formula plus one-variable cubic proves the spherical-volume optimum. Exact edge constraints give the uniform optimum, and strict inequalities plus asymptotic Taylor expansions prove all comparison and limit claims. Standalone directly reconstructs 28 orders of support planes, angles and volumes, passing 261044 checks. Experiments are corroborative only.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Antipodal counts, illumination numbers, and ellipsoid volumes contain no adjacent-facet normal-angle optimization. The bipyramid theorem concerns n+2 vertices and 2n triangular faces, whereas antiprisms have 2n vertices and two polygonal plus 2n triangular faces; no affine/dual reduction preserves the interior-dihedral optimization. In fact their optimal large-order maxima tend to pi and 2pi/3 respectively. The present claim is not a special case of those results.

value.rationale: Motivated by the 2026 sharp general dihedral-threshold question, the finding computes a sharp angular barrier for a natural infinite polytope family, with a unique equidihedral equality geometry. Unlike isolated angle substitutions, it proves the strict incompatibility of three standard shape selectors for all n>=4, gives exact angular penalties and shows qualitatively distinct n^-2, n^-1 and n^0 aspect-ratio scales with an asymptotic pi/3 angle loss. The exact comparison answers a natural optimization-versus-uniformity question and is not a mere table recomputation.
